name: Armenian
rationale: Holds Classical-Middle, Eastern and Western Armenian; WALS genus Armenian coincides (1/1 mapped) and Indo-European handbooks treat this branch as 'Armenian', parallel to 'Albanian' for alba1267 in this dataset.
sources: https://wals.info/languoid/genus/armenian;https://glottolog.org/resource/languoid/id/arme1241

name: Aztecan
rationale: The genus holds all Nahuatl varieties, Pipil and Pochutec, and matches WALS genus Aztecan (10 of 11 mapped members). "Aztecan" (or Nahuan) is the usual name for this branch of Uto-Aztecan; "Aztec" names a people, not a language group.
sources: https://wals.info/languoid/genus/aztecan; Campbell 1997, American Indian Languages (OUP); https://glottolog.org/resource/languoid/id/azte1234

name: North-West Bantu
rationale: Bostoen explicitly applies this name to zone A plus B10/(20)/30, closely matching the genus. Membership is only approximate: treatments differ over Mbam and B20, so this is a provisional conventional label rather than a verified exact synonym.
sources: Bostoen 2008, Bantu Spirantization: Morphologization, lexicalization and historical classification, p. 304, https://www.africamuseum.be/publication_docs/Bostoen%202008%20Diachronica.pdf; Bostoen and Grégoire 2007, La question bantoue: bilan et perspectives, https://backoffice.biblio.ugent.be/download/446279/8675570; Bostoen and Guérois 2022, Reconstructing suffixal phrasemes in Bantu verbal derivation, pp. 363–364, https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.7575829

name: Bolivia-Paraná
rationale: The genus holds Mojeño (Ignaciano, Trinitario), Baure, Paunaka, Apolista, Magiana and Terena-Kinikinao-Chané, and matches WALS genus Bolivia-Parana (3/3). Terena and Chané are spoken in Brazil and Argentina, so "Bolivian" is too narrow.
sources: https://wals.info/languoid/genus/boliviaparana; Aikhenvald 1999, The Arawak language family, in Dixon & Aikhenvald (eds.) The Amazonian Languages

name: Central Pacific
rationale: Glottolog 'linkage' is a bookkeeping label. The group (Fijian, Rotuman and Polynesian) is called Central Pacific throughout the Oceanic literature.
sources: https://glottolog.org/resource/languoid/id/cent2060;Lynch, Ross & Crowley 2002, The Oceanic Languages;Geraghty 1983, The History of the Fijian Languages

name: Nyun-Buy
rationale: The genus holds the Bainounk (Nyun) varieties plus Buy (Kasanga, Kobiana); 'Nyun' alone normally denotes only the Bainounk cluster, whereas the specialist name for the whole group is Nyun-Buy.
sources: Pozdniakov & Segerer 2024, A genealogical classification of Atlantic languages, in Lüpke (ed.), The Oxford Guide to the Atlantic Languages of West Africa, sect. 'The Nyun-Buy cluster' (https://academic.oup.com/book/59850/chapter/511367287);https://glottolog.org/resource/languoid/id/east2703

name: Hungarian
rationale: Holds only Hungarian and Old Hungarian; 'Hungaric' is a Glottolog formation, and the literature simply speaks of Hungarian (the Uralic handbook's Hungarian chapter covers its history).
sources: https://glottolog.org/resource/languoid/id/hung1287;Abondolo & Valijärvi (eds.) 2023, The Uralic Languages, 2nd ed. (Routledge)

name: Kra
rationale: Holds only the Kra branch (Eastern Kra and Southwestern Kra: Gelao varieties, Lachi, Laha, Buyang, Qabiao, En), but 'Kadai/Kadaic' is widely used for the whole Tai-Kadai (Kra-Dai) family; 'Kra' is the established name for this branch since Ostapirat (2000), which Glottolog itself cites for the node.
sources: https://glottolog.org/resource/languoid/id/kada1291;Ostapirat 2000, Proto-Kra, Linguistics of the Tibeto-Burman Area 23(1)

name: Khanty
rationale: Holds the Khanty varieties (Northern, Eastern/Surgut-Vach-Vasjugan, Southern) that Glottolog treats as languages; specialists call this group 'Khanty' (e.g. the Khanty chapter in the Uralic handbook), 'Khantyic' being a Glottolog formation.
sources: https://glottolog.org/resource/languoid/id/khan1279;Csepregi 2023, Khanty, in Abondolo & Valijärvi (eds.), The Uralic Languages, 2nd ed. (Routledge)

name: Korap
rationale: Drop the Glottolog 'linkage' label. The genus holds Arop-Lokep, Karnai, Malasanga and Mur Pano, which make up Ross's Korap group of Ngero-Vitiaz.
sources: https://glottolog.org/resource/languoid/id/kora1297;Ross 1988, Proto Oceanic and the Austronesian Languages of Western Melanesia;Lynch, Ross & Crowley 2002, The Oceanic Languages;https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/North_New_Guinea_languages

name: Mansi
rationale: Holds Northern, Central and Southern Mansi; specialists call this group 'Mansi' (e.g. the Mansi chapter in the Uralic handbook), 'Mansic' being a Glottolog formation.
sources: https://glottolog.org/resource/languoid/id/mans1269;Virtanen & Horváth 2023, Mansi, in Abondolo & Valijärvi (eds.), The Uralic Languages, 2nd ed. (Routledge)

name: Maká-Nivaclé
rationale: Mataguayo I is a Glottolog bookkeeping label. The genus holds Maká and Nivaclé, and the literature calls this proposed clade Maká-Nivaclé. Nikulin & Carol 2024 doubt that it is a clade.
sources: Nikulin & Carol 2024, Historical phonology of Mataguayan (Language Science Press); https://glottolog.org/resource/languoid/id/mata1290

name: Wichí-Chorote
rationale: Mataguayo II is a Glottolog bookkeeping label. The genus holds Wichí (Weenhayek, Güisnay, Vejoz) and Chorote (Forest and Riverine), the well-supported Wichí-Chorote (Chorote-Wichí) clade of Mataguayan.
sources: Nikulin & Carol 2024, Historical phonology of Mataguayan (Language Science Press; https://zenodo.org/records/13907413); https://glottolog.org/resource/languoid/id/mata1291

name: Munda
rationale: Holds the Munda languages (North Munda, Kharia, Juang, Sora-Juray-Gorum, Gutob-Remo, Gata'); all 9 WALS-mapped members of WALS genus Munda fall here, and 'Munda' is the universal name in the specialist literature, while 'Mundaic' is a Glottolog-only form.
sources: https://wals.info/languoid/genus/munda;https://glottolog.org/resource/languoid/id/mund1335;Anderson (ed.) 2008, The Munda Languages (Routledge)

name: Talodi
rationale: 'Narrow' is Glottolog bookkeeping distinguishing the group from older Talodi including Lafofa (Tegem, a separate genus here); the genus coincides with WALS genus Talodi (2/2) and is the group called Talodi in the specialist literature. Whole-family genus, hence medium.
sources: https://wals.info/languoid/genus/talodi;Norton & Alaki 2015, The Talodi languages: a comparative-historical analysis, Occasional Papers in the Study of Sudanese Languages 11;https://glottolog.org/resource/languoid/id/narr1279

name: North Huon Gulf
rationale: Drop the Glottolog 'linkage' label. The genus holds Bugawac, Kela and Yabem, which make up North Huon Gulf in Ross's Huon Gulf family.
sources: https://glottolog.org/resource/languoid/id/nort2858;Ross 1988, Proto Oceanic and the Austronesian Languages of Western Melanesia;Lynch, Ross & Crowley 2002, The Oceanic Languages

name: Nuclear Papuan Tip
rationale: Drop the Glottolog 'linkage' label. Keep 'Nuclear', which is part of Ross's established name and contrasts with Peripheral Papuan Tip. The genus holds the North Papuan Mainland-D'Entrecasteaux and Suauic languages.
sources: https://glottolog.org/resource/languoid/id/nucl1744;Ross 1988, Proto Oceanic and the Austronesian Languages of Western Melanesia;Lynch, Ross & Crowley 2002, The Oceanic Languages

name: Permic
rationale: Holds Komi (Zyrian, Permyak, Yazva) and Udmurt, exactly WALS genus Permic (3/3 mapped); 'Permic' is the standard English term in Uralistics and avoids the geological sense of 'Permian'.
sources: https://wals.info/languoid/genus/permic;https://glottolog.org/resource/languoid/id/perm1256;Abondolo & Valijärvi (eds.) 2023, The Uralic Languages, 2nd ed. (Routledge)

name: Kampan
rationale: The genus is exactly the Kampa/Campa languages (Asháninka, Ashéninka varieties, Caquinte, Machiguenga, Nanti, Nomatsiguenga). "Pre-Andine" in Aikhenvald's usage also covers Yanesha' (Amuesha), which is a separate genus here. WALS calls these 4/4 mapped members "Pre-Andine Arawakan", but specialists name the group Kampa(n).
sources: Mihas 2017, The Kampa subgroup of the Arawak language family, in Aikhenvald & Dixon (eds.) Cambridge Handbook of Linguistic Typology (https://researchonline.jcu.edu.au/47586/); https://wals.info/languoid/genus/preandinearawakan

name: South Bird's Head Proper
rationale: The genus holds the South Bird's Head family minus Inanwatanic (Kaburi, Kais, Puragi, Kemberano, Kokoda/Arandai, Dombano); WALS calls exactly this group "South Bird's Head Proper" (its only WALS member, Arandai, is here), and plain "South Bird's Head" would wrongly suggest the whole family including Inanwatan.
sources: https://wals.info/languoid/genus/southbirdsheadproper; https://glottolog.org/resource/languoid/id/sout1516

name: Tabar
rationale: Drop the Glottolog 'linkage' label. The genus holds Lihir, Mandara and Notsi, Ross's Tabar group. Confidence is medium because 'Tabar' is also an alternative name of Mandara, a member language.
sources: https://glottolog.org/resource/languoid/id/taba1270;Ross 1988, Proto Oceanic and the Austronesian Languages of Western Melanesia;Lynch, Ross & Crowley 2002, The Oceanic Languages

name: Tsimshianic
rationale: The genus is the whole family (Nisga'a, Gitxsan, Coast/Southern Tsimshian) and matches WALS genus Tsimshianic (3/3). "Tsimshian" is also the name of one member language (Sm'algyax).
sources: https://wals.info/languoid/genus/tsimshianic; Mithun 1999, The Languages of Native North America (CUP); Campbell 1997, American Indian Languages

name: Caribbean Arawakan (unclassified)
rationale: This is a Glottolog bookkeeping node for Araicu and Uirina, which are left unclassified within Caribbean Arawakan. It is not a subgroup.
sources: https://glottolog.org/resource/languoid/id/uncl1521

name: Indo-European (unclassified)
rationale: A Glottolog bookkeeping node for poorly attested Indo-European languages not placed in any branch (Dacian, Messapic, Thracian); it is not a subgroup.
sources: https://glottolog.org/resource/languoid/id/uncl1527

name: Maxakalian (unclassified)
rationale: This is a Glottolog bookkeeping node for poorly attested Maxakalian languages (Capoxo, Koropó, Macuni) left unclassified within Nuclear Maxakalian. It is not a subgroup.
sources: https://glottolog.org/resource/languoid/id/unun9898

name: Benue-Congo (unclassified)
rationale: Glottolog pseudo-family node for languages unclassified within Benue-Congo (here Baissa Fali and Tita); it is not a subgroup, so the name should say so transparently.
sources: https://glottolog.org/resource/languoid/id/unun9910

name: Southern Uto-Aztecan (unclassified)
rationale: This is a Glottolog bookkeeping node for the poorly attested Coca and Jova, which are left unclassified within Southern Uto-Aztecan. It is not a subgroup.
sources: https://glottolog.org/resource/languoid/id/unun9947

name: Rai Coast (unclassified)
rationale: Glottolog bookkeeping node for Rai Coast languages without a subgroup assignment (Biyom, Tauya); it is not a subgroup, and the transparent name avoids implying one.
sources: https://glottolog.org/resource/languoid/id/unun9972; Pawley & Hammarström 2017, The Trans New Guinea family (in Palmer ed., The Languages and Linguistics of the New Guinea Area)

name: Willaumez
rationale: Drop the Glottolog 'linkage' label. The genus holds Bola, Bulu, Meramera and Nakanai, which make up Ross's Willaumez group of Meso-Melanesian.
sources: https://glottolog.org/resource/languoid/id/will1243;Ross 1988, Proto Oceanic and the Austronesian Languages of Western Melanesia;Lynch, Ross & Crowley 2002, The Oceanic Languages;https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Meso-Melanesian_languages

name: Yolngu
rationale: The genus is the whole Yolngu (Yolŋu Matha) group (Dhuwal, Djambarrpuyngu, Gupapuyngu, Gumatj, Ritharrngu, Djinang, Djinba, Dhangu, Dayi, Nhangu); specialists and Glottolog's own child node "Southern Yolngu" use the spelling Yolngu/Yolŋu, while "Yuulngu" is an older spelling.
sources: https://glottolog.org/resource/languoid/id/yuul1239; Wilkinson 1991, Djambarrpuyngu: a Yolngu variety of northern Australia (PhD, Sydney); Bowern & Atkinson 2012, Computational phylogenetics and the internal structure of Pama-Nyungan, Language 88(4)
